react_result.final_narrative_text: The treatment-versus-control differential metabolome converges on two interlocked biochemical systems: one-carbon/methionine metabolism and arachidonic acid–mediated lipid signaling. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — multi-database ORA (RaMP), empirical-compound m/z-network activity (Mummichog), and KEGG-specific pathway-set enrichment (MetaboAnalystR) — the top-scoring pathway is consistently Methionine and Cysteine Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270 / KEGG:map00270 / MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism). Four driver metabolites (L-methionine C00073, S-adenosyl-L-methionine C00019, homocysteine C00155, and cysteic acid C00506) are simultaneously identified as pathway members by all three tools, with fold-enrichment values exceeding 577 and FDR-corrected p-values below 1.2 × 10⁻¹³. The methionine cycle links directly into methyl-donor biochemistry through S-adenosylmethionine, and its downstream product homocysteine feeds the transsulfuration pathway where cysteic acid (the oxidative product of cysteine) appears. Adenosine (C00212) is also present as the cleavage product of S-adenosylmethionine. Choline (C00114) and L-threonine (C00188) additionally map to the broader Glycine, Serine and Threonine Metabolism super-pathway (KEGG:hsa00260), reinforced by Mummichog at rank 0 (p = 0.013). A secondary signal emerges from the lipidome: 15-HETE (C04742) and 8(S)-HPETE (C14823) map to Arachidonic Acid Metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, rank 1), with 15-HETE also confirmed in MetaboAnalystR's Glycerophospholipid metabolism branch (p = 0.062). The convergent pathway architecture — one-carbon folate/methionine routing driving homocysteine transsulfuration, simultaneously producing methyl groups that modulate phospholipid membrane remodeling linked to eicosanoid generation — defines a biologically coherent phenotype shift.

RaMP-DB multi-database ORA identified Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) as the top-ranking pathway (FDR = 3.75 × 10⁻¹⁹, fold-enrichment = 689.5) with eight input metabolites as members: homocysteine, S-adenosyl-L-methionine, L-methionine, choline, L-glutamic acid, adenosine, (R)-lipoic acid, and L-threonine. The same method placed Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:map00270, FDR = 1.19 × 10⁻¹³, fold-enrichment = 578.0) at rank 4, and the WikiPathways Methionine de novo and salvage pathway (WP:WP3580, FDR = 1.16 × 10⁻¹³) at rank 3. Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis independently confirmed amino-acid metabolism pathways, ranking Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism and Methionine and cysteine metabolism as its top hits (both p = 0.0168), and also detected Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as a lipid-oxidative signalling layer involving 15-HETE and 8(S)-HPETE. Across both paradigms, L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), homocysteine (KEGG:C00155), and S-adenosyl-L-methionine (KEGG:C00019) are verified members of KEGG:map00270 and KEGG:map00260; choline (KEGG:C00114) and L-threonine (KEGG:C00188) are confirmed in the same glycine/serine cluster. The convergent pathway architecture defines a biologically coherent phenotype centered on sulfur amino-acid flux and one-carbon metabolism with a secondary lipid-oxidative signalling component.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks it first (FDR 3.7e-19, fold enrichment 690, 8 of 13 metabolites mapped) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA corroborates with p=0.0204. The mummichog m/z-direct network independently returns Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism as its top hit with full 8-of-8 metabolite overlap, confirming the signal across compound ID resolution paradigms. A secondary convergent axis around one-carbon methionine flux is supported by RaMP ORA for KEGG:map00270 Methionine Metabolism (FDR 1.2e-13, 6 metabolites) and MetaboAnalystR for hsa00670 (p=3.36e-07, 5 metabolites). Driver metabolites spanning both axes are L-methionine (KEGG:C00073), S-adenosyl-L-methionine (KEGG:C00019), L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00155), and L-threonine (KEGG:C00188). The biological phenotype implicates joint disruption of amino-acid donor metabolism and connected one-carbon cycling, with choline and adenosine acting as upstream inputs to the methionine Salvage branch.
